title: Ethiopian Chickpea Flour Stew
community: All of Ethiopia — the quickest and most beloved fasting dish
author: Mama Tigist

heritage.origin: All of Ethiopia — the fasting dish that can be made in 25 minutes
heritage.history: Shiro is the roasted and spiced chickpea (or broad bean) flour that is the foundation of Shiro Wat — Ethiopia's most practical fasting dish. The shiro powder, already containing berbere and other spices, is simply stirred into a base of sautéed onion and water until it forms a smooth, thick stew. It can be made in 25 minutes, requires minimal ingredients, and is extraordinarily satisfying. There are two main varieties: thick shiro (firfir) and thin shiro. Shiro is the food that urban Ethiopians eat most frequently during the 200+ annual fasting days.

desc: Ethiopian Shiro Wat — spiced roasted chickpea flour stirred into a sauce of sautéed onion, garlic, and water until smooth and thick. The quickest Ethiopian main course — done in 25 minutes, deeply satisfying, and the most frequently eaten fasting dish in the country.
longDesc: Shiro Wat is the weekday solution to Ethiopian fasting — while Misir Wat takes an hour and Kik Alicha takes longer, Shiro takes 25 minutes. The shiro powder (pre-spiced roasted chickpea flour) is simply stirred into a sautéed onion base with water until thick and smooth. Eaten with injera, it is one of the most satisfying mouthfuls in Ethiopian cooking.
ingredients: 1 cup shiro powder (spiced roasted chickpea flour)
1 tsp berbere (ETH091) — optional, for extra heat
// Homemade shiro powder: roast and grind chickpeas + berbere + spices
steps: Heat oil in a saucepan. Cook onion until very golden — 10 minutes.
Add extra berbere if using. Stir 30 seconds.
Add water. Bring to a simmer.
Whisk shiro powder gradually into the simmering water — add slowly to prevent lumps.
Stir continuously over medium heat for 12—15 minutes until very smooth and thick.
The shiro should be pourable but thick.
chefTips: Whisk the shiro powder in gradually — adding all at once creates lumps.
Stir continuously — shiro sticks to the bottom easily.
Thick shiro (less water) is called firfir-style; thin shiro (more water) is also traditional.
Add a piece of kibbeh on non-fasting days — transforms it from good to great.
Shiro powder can be bought at Ethiopian grocery stores or made at home.
commonMistakes: Adding powder all at once — lumps.
Too thin — should be thick enough to scoop with injera.
cookingScience: Shiro powder is pre-cooked through roasting — the chickpea starch has already been partially gelatinised. When added to simmering water, this pre-gelatinised starch hydrates rapidly into a smooth paste without the lumping problems of raw starch. The continuous stirring distributes heat evenly and prevents the high-starch mixture from scorching.
sustainabilityTips: Chickpeas fix nitrogen in soil — one of the most sustainable protein crops.
Shiro powder stores for months without refrigeration — minimal food waste.
healthBenefits: The berbere in shiro powder adds antioxidants.
Good source of iron and folate.
culturalNote: Shiro Wat is the everyday miracle of Ethiopian fasting cuisine — the dish that makes 200+ days of plant-based eating not just bearable but genuinely delicious. Every Ethiopian home has shiro powder in the pantry. It is the last-resort meal, the quick weekday lunch, and the beloved constant of fasting life.
